newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina extends appropriations again.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina extends appropriations again.

text.p: In the absence of a budget agreement, the North Carolina General Assembly extended budget appropriations at fiscal 1997 levels for another two weeks.
The House voted 110-0 Thursday to extend the appropriations through Aug. 15. The measure previosuly had passed the Senate and now goes to Gov. Jim Hunt, who was expected to quickly sign it.
The Democrat-dominated Senate and Rebpublican-controlled House are still at odds over the $11.4 billion budget for the fiscal year that began July 1.

Lawmakers previously extended the appropriations through July 31 when it became apparent they would not reach agreement by the start of the new budget year. The extension allows the state government to keep operatingd but delays raises and spending hikes.
The House and Senate remain at odds over the allocation of Medicaid funds and federal welfare dollars.
